Maya Chen: Maya Chen: Before we finish, can we confirm who will put together the readiness checklist for the next rollout discussion?
Jordan Lee: Jordan Lee: I can prepare the first draft of the rollout readiness checklist. I will collect the checks we already use and flag anything that still needs an owner.
Priya Shah: Priya Shah: That would help. We should make sure the list covers support readiness as well as the technical checks, but I do not think we have agreed the final sections yet.
Maya Chen: Maya Chen: Good. Let's treat the checklist as a draft for now. We can review it together at the next planning meeting and confirm what is still missing.
Jordan Lee: Jordan Lee: Understood. I will bring the draft and the open questions to that review; I am not assigning the unresolved items on behalf of the group.
Maya Chen: Maya Chen: Let's anchor the discussion on scope and expected outcome. What has actually changed since the last check-in?
Jordan Lee: Jordan Lee: The current picture is the first draft covers owners and milestones but does not yet include escalation paths. We have the draft has a short list of milestones and open questions, and the signal I am watching is the group needs to identify missing handoff steps before treating the checklist as complete.
Priya Shah: Priya Shah: My concern is assigning unresolved checklist items now could imply commitments that the group has not agreed. If the relevant owners need to confirm which handoff steps apply, what do we tell the people relying on this work?
Sam Rivera: Sam Rivera: We can keep unresolved items marked as questions and review them with the relevant owners. We should keep which escalation contacts should be listed for after-hours support visible until that check is complete.
